Guide to Editing and Shiny Inputs

Source: vignettes/edition.Rmd
edition.Rmd

New in v0.4.5.9000

This guide describes the reactableEdit extensions: native editing, server-side validation, individual IDs, observers, updates, disabling inputs, row actions, and tooltips. The code snippets are intended for a Shiny application; a complete example that runs without requiring you to invent business logic appears at the end.

Load library(reactableEdit), not library(reactable). Function names retain their original names. Do not load both packages or mix their widgets in the same HTML document.

1. Overview: Which API should you use?

Need API
Need API
:– :–
Build the table reactable(), reactableOutput(), renderReactable()
Configure a column input colDef(editable, editor, editorOptions, inputId, ...)
Read a specific cell input[[id]], observeEvent(input[[id]], ...)
Handle all submissions getReactableEdit(outputId)
Accept, normalize, or reject resolveReactableEdit(outputId, edit, ...)
Change a mounted input’s value or options The Shiny update*Input() function for its type
Disable a mounted input updateReactableInput(session, inputId, disabled)
Disable cells, including off-page cells disabledInputs in reactable() or updateReactable()
Request add/remove controls rowActions in reactable() or updateReactable()
Observe a row action getReactableRowAction(outputId)
Provide a new row or reject its creation addReactableRow(outputId, ...)
Create a rich tooltip reactableTooltip(content, ...)
Add a column or header tooltip colDef(tooltip, headerTooltip)
Add a row, cell, or header tooltip tooltips in reactable() or updateReactable()
Update a mounted input’s tooltip updateReactableTooltip(session, inputId, tooltip)
Translate labels and announcements reactableLang()
Read the page, sorting, or selection getReactableState()

Three states to distinguish

  1. Server data: your source of truth, such as a reactiveVal(), file, or database.
  2. Confirmed browser data: used by the table and updated after acceptance.
  3. Input draft: the value being entered, not yet saved and not necessarily valid.

A Shiny input is not a database. Reading input[[id]] does not mean that its value has been accepted. With server-side validation, save the value first, then call resolveReactableEdit().

2. Build an editable table

Shiny output and stable keys 

library(shiny)
library(reactableEdit)

cars <- MASS::Cars93[1:6, c("Manufacturer", "Model", "Type", "Price")]
cars$id <- paste0("car", seq_len(nrow(cars)))
cars$Manufacturer <- as.character(cars$Manufacturer)
cars$Model <- as.character(cars$Model)
cars$Type <- as.character(cars$Type)
cars$Available <- TRUE
cars$CheckedOn <- as.Date("2026-01-01")
cars$Notes <- ""

# In the UI:
reactableOutput("cars")

# In the server:
output$cars <- renderReactable({
  reactable(
    cars,
    rowId = "id",
    columns = list(
      id = colDef(show = FALSE),
      Manufacturer = colDef(editable = TRUE),
      Price = colDef(editable = TRUE, editor = "number")
    )
  )
})

rowId refers to a data column, not a displayed row number. Keys must be unique and non-missing: strings or integers exactly representable in JavaScript, between -(2^53 - 1) and 2^53 - 1. Prefer simple keys such as "car1" or a database ID.

The key column can be hidden, but it cannot be editable. Do not regenerate its values after sorting, deleting, or paginating. A row edit must always be looked up by its key.

reactableOutput() creates the Shiny HTML output. renderReactable() supplies its contents. reactable() builds the table definition; its new parameters are rowId, inputIdPrefix, disabledInputs, rowActions, and tooltips.

Editing parameters for colDef()

Parameter Default Description
editable FALSE Displays a real Shiny input that is always visible
editor "text" Selects one of the six editors
editorOptions NULL Options for the corresponding Shiny constructor
inputId NULL A specific ID or a function of the row key and column name
editValidation TRUE Waits for server acceptance or rejection
editStatus "icon" "icon", "text", or "none" indicator
editStatusDuration 2000 Success duration in milliseconds; 0 keeps it until the next edit
inputDisabled FALSE Disables the column’s inputs by default
tooltip NULL A cell tooltip, fixed or calculated at construction
headerTooltip NULL A header tooltip

These parameters can be shared through defaultColDef. Note: defaultColDef = colDef(editable = TRUE) also makes the key editable unless its column explicitly sets editable = FALSE. A native editor cannot be combined with a cell renderer on the same column.

The six input types

editor Shiny constructor Expected data Example options
"text" textInput() Text or compatible scalar values placeholder, width
"number" numericInput() Finite numbers or missing values min, max, step, width
"select" selectInput() Values present in the choices choices, width
"checkbox" checkboxInput() Non-missing logical values width
"date" dateInput() Date or ISO YYYY-MM-DD strings min, max, format, language, weekstart
"textarea" textAreaInput() Text or compatible scalar values rows, cols, placeholder, resize 
columns <- list(
  id = colDef(show = FALSE),
  Manufacturer = colDef(
    editable = TRUE, editor = "text", editorOptions = list(placeholder = "Manufacturer")
  ),
  Type = colDef(
    editable = TRUE, editor = "select", editorOptions = list(choices = unique(cars$Type))
  ),
  Price = colDef(
    editable = TRUE, editor = "number", editorOptions = list(min = 0, step = 0.01)
  ),
  Available = colDef(editable = TRUE, editor = "checkbox"),
  CheckedOn = colDef(
    editable = TRUE, editor = "date", editorOptions = list(language = "en", format = "mm/dd/yyyy")
  ),
  Notes = colDef(editable = TRUE, editor = "textarea", editorOptions = list(rows = 2))
)

editorOptions uses the arguments of the constructor, not those of an update*Input() function. inputId, label, value, selected, multiple, selectize, and updateOn are managed by the package and cannot be supplied here. The select is native, single-choice, and does not use Selectize; choices is required.

HTML constraints such as min can help with data entry, but never replace server-side checks. An empty value from a number or date editor can be represented as NULL in the global protocol.

3. IDs: table, row, column, and input

Automatic format

For reactableOutput("cars"), with the key "car1" and the "Price" column:

cars_car1_Price

The format is <prefix>_<encoded row key>_<encoded column name>. The prefix defaults to the output ID. The row/column components are encoded with JavaScript’s encodeURIComponent; a space becomes %20. For an ID containing special characters, use input[[id]], not $ notation.

IDs are case-sensitive. The key is converted to a string. Non-editable cells do not have an individual Shiny input binding. Group rows are not data inputs.

Change the prefix 

reactable(cars, rowId = "id", columns = columns, inputIdPrefix = "edit")
# The first Price cell becomes: edit_car1_Price

Choose different prefixes for multiple tables. All IDs on the page, including those of other Shiny widgets, must be unique. Collisions are reported: the package does not silently rename IDs.

Customize specific cells 

colDef(
  editable = TRUE,
  editor = "number",
  inputId = function(rowId, columnId) {
    if (rowId == "car1") "main_price" else NULL
  }
)

The function receives the stable key and column name. Returning NULL keeps the automatic ID. A constant ID such as inputId = "main_price" is suitable for only one cell: using it across multiple rows would create duplicates.

Custom IDs cannot contain spaces or colons. Prefer letters, numbers, and underscores. R ID callbacks are evaluated for rows at construction time, not each time a row is added in the browser. For a new row, use addReactableRow(inputIds = ...) or keep the automatic ID.

Global event IDs 

cars__reactable__edit        edit event
cars__reactable__row_action  add/remove event

Use the public helpers getReactableEdit() and getReactableRowAction() rather than reconstructing these names. edit$inputId contains the browser’s actual ID, including any module namespace. Do not pass it directly to an updater using the module session: the session would add the namespace again.

4. When is an edit submitted?

Editor Submission
Text / number Enter or blur; Tab submits and moves focus
Multiline text Ctrl+Enter / Cmd+Enter or blur; Enter alone inserts a line
Select / checkbox As soon as the value changes
Date Enter, blur, or selection in the calendar

Text is not submitted on every keystroke. An unchanged value does not create a new edit. Local validation occurs on submission, not while typing. A locally invalid entry may be rejected before any server event.

Escape restores the confirmed value without creating a global edit event. The individual input may still be updated to reflect this restoration. If a tooltip is open, the first Escape closes it; the second has the editor’s usual behavior.

While validation is pending, the same cell cannot be submitted again. Text, number, and textarea editors are read-only; the other editors are temporarily disabled. Drafts and errors follow the cell key when changing pages or when virtualized rows are remounted.

5. input[[id]] and observeEvent()

Observe a specific cell 

observeEvent(input$cars_car1_Price, {
  value <- input$cars_car1_Price
  message("Native value received: ", value)
}, ignoreInit = TRUE)

id <- "cars_car1_Price"
observeEvent(input[[id]], {
  message("Targeted input: ", id, " = ", input[[id]])
}, ignoreInit = TRUE)

ignoreInit = TRUE prevents the observer from running when it is created. It does not guarantee that an initial value sent later, when an input is mounted or remounted, will be ignored. ignoreNULL = FALSE allows you to process null values if your logic requires it.

A mounted input publishes its initial value. It may also publish after a submission, an Escape restoration, or a server update. Remounting may restore a value that was already known. Native functions retain their Shiny types: notably, logical for checkboxes and Date for dates.

An individual observer is therefore not a reliable detector of an accepted user change. Use it for display or related calculations. To validate and save edits, prefer the global event, which carries the row key, column, and submission ID. Do not save the same edit twice using both observers.

Observe several known IDs 

observers <- lapply(c("cars_car1_Price", "cars_car2_Price"), function(id) {
  force(id)
  observeEvent(input[[id]], {
    message(id, " : ", input[[id]])
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE)
})

session$onSessionEnded(function() {
  lapply(observers, function(observer) observer$destroy())
})

Each observer must capture its own ID. For dynamically added rows, create the observer when the key is known and destroy it when the row is removed. Avoid recreating all observers on every edit. The global protocol avoids this problem entirely and also covers new rows.

6. Server-side validation and saving

getReactableEdit() 

getReactableEdit(outputId, session = NULL)

Reactively returns NULL before the first submission, then the most recently received edit:

Field Meaning
editId Unique ID for this submission
inputId Full browser input ID
rowId Stable row key as a string
columnId Column name
oldValue Value confirmed in the browser before submission
value Proposed value; dates are ISO strings

oldValue describes the browser, not necessarily the current state of your database. For multiple users, also check permissions and conflicts with server data. The helper exposes the latest edit, not a history; maintain your own log if needed.

observeEvent(getReactableEdit("cars"), {
  edit <- getReactableEdit("cars")
  # Validate, save, then respond. See the complete example at the end of the guide.
}, ignoreInit = TRUE)

resolveReactableEdit() 

resolveReactableEdit(
  outputId, edit, value = edit$value, error = NULL, session = NULL
)
resolveReactableEdit("cars", edit)                       # Accept the submitted value
resolveReactableEdit("cars", edit, value = 25.50)         # Accept a normalized value
resolveReactableEdit("cars", edit, error = "Price rejected") # Reject
resolveReactableEdit("cars", edit, value = NULL)          # Accept a missing number/date

The response must include the edit object for the relevant submission. The browser correlates the response with editId, inputId, row, and column; a stale response cannot accept another edit. Acceptance updates the browser’s confirmed data and displays the configured success indicator. Rejection keeps the confirmed value, leaves the proposed value available for correction, and displays the error.

value must be a valid JSON scalar: text, finite number, logical, Date, or NULL. Do not use NA, NaN, Inf, a vector, or a list as an accepted value. error must be non-empty text; with error = NULL, the value is accepted.

Every submission with validation enabled requires a response. Without a call to resolveReactableEdit(), the cell remains pending. An updateNumericInput() is not an acceptance. If saving fails, report the failure explicitly; do not show success for a write that did not happen. Asynchronous operations must retain the original edit object until they respond.

Avoid rebuilding the table on every save 

saved <- reactiveVal(cars)
tbl <- reactable(cars, rowId = "id", columns = columns)
output$cars <- renderReactable(tbl)
output$saved <- renderTable(saved())

In the global observer, update saved(), then respond with resolveReactableEdit(). Avoid renderReactable(reactable(saved(), ...)) for this workflow: each save rebuilds the widget, clears drafts, and may invalidate pending requests.

editValidation = FALSE 

colDef(editable = TRUE, editor = "textarea", editValidation = FALSE)

The submission is applied immediately to the browser data. The native input and global event are still sent to Shiny, but resolutions are ignored and no server-validation checkmark is shown. This does not save anything automatically.

Reserve this mode for a local application or a field whose processing does not require this protocol. To reject a value applied locally, the application must send a corrective value itself or replace the data. This is not equivalent to server-side validation.

7. Native server-side update*Input() functions

Which function for which editor?

The following snippets assume that the cells are mounted and use the columns from section 2:

updateTextInput(session, "cars_car1_Manufacturer", value = "Acura")
updateNumericInput(session, "cars_car1_Price", value = 25, min = 0, max = 100, step = 0.5)
updateSelectInput(session, "cars_car1_Type", choices = unique(cars$Type), selected = cars$Type[1])
updateCheckboxInput(session, "cars_car1_Available", value = FALSE)
updateDateInput(session, "cars_car1_CheckedOn", value = as.Date("2026-02-01"))
updateTextAreaInput(session, "cars_car1_Notes", value = "Updated note")

# Change an option without changing the value:
updateTextInput(session, "cars_car1_Manufacturer", placeholder = "Expected name")

The native function signatures are unchanged. Use selected, not value, for updateSelectInput(). Available options depend on the function and Shiny version. updateSelectizeInput() and updaters for unlisted widgets do not target these native editors.

A server-side value update republishes the individual input and, unless an edit is pending, also updates the table data in the browser. It does not create a global edit event or an acceptance checkmark. Update your server-side source in the same operation to keep it consistent.

Changing the choices for a select does not automatically change your server-side business rules. A selected value changed by the updater remains a server update, not a user edit. While a request is pending, prefer resolveReactableEdit(value = ...) over sending two competing commands.

Mounted cell or off-page?

An input is mounted when it exists in the DOM: pagination, filtering, collapsing a group, and virtualization can remove it. ID-based commands are not persistently queued for an absent input. An old value in input[[id]] does not prove that the input is still mounted.

To change off-page values, update the server-side source and then use updateReactable(data = ...). For off-page disabling and tooltips, use the table rules disabledInputs and tooltips. A native option changed by ID, such as choices or a placeholder, is not a new column definition and does not benefit from the special persistence for disabled and tooltip overrides.

8. Disable and re-enable inputs

Column, row, and cell 

colDef(editable = TRUE, editor = "checkbox", inputDisabled = TRUE)

rules <- list(
  rows = c("car1", "car2"),
  columns = "Price",
  cells = list(
    car1 = list(Price = FALSE), # Exception: allow this price
    car3 = c("Notes", "Type")   # Disable these cells
  )
)
reactable(cars, rowId = "id", columns = columns, disabledInputs = rules)
updateReactable("cars", disabledInputs = rules)

Priority order:

  1. Individual command by ID or external change to the disabled attribute.
  2. Cell rule TRUE or FALSE.
  3. Row, column, or colDef(inputDisabled = TRUE) disabling: any one is sufficient.

FALSE for a cell is a true exception that enables it. Rules use stable keys, not positions. They can target off-page cells or a key that will be added later.

updateReactableInput() 

updateReactableInput(
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain(), inputId, disabled = TRUE
)
updateReactableInput(session, "cars_car1_Price")                   # Disable
updateReactableInput(session, "cars_car1_Price", disabled = FALSE) # Re-enable

session$sendInputMessage("cars_car1_Price", list(value = 35, disabled = TRUE))

This helper does not change the value. It targets a mounted input, and its override persists after remounting and replacing only the data. A server can change the value of a disabled input. Native update*Input() functions do not gain a disabled argument: use this helper or a message.

Reset rules and overrides 

updateReactable("cars", disabledInputs = NULL)   # Leave unchanged
updateReactable("cars", disabledInputs = list()) # Clear rules and ID overrides

Each non-NULL list replaces the previous rules and clears individual overrides. colDef(inputDisabled = TRUE) defaults remain: clearing the rules does not necessarily make everything editable. Keep your rule list on the server if you want to change only one entry.

Disabling cancels an unsubmitted draft and restores the confirmed value without a global submission. An edit that is already pending may complete, but its response does not re-enable the field.

With shinyjs 

# In the UI:
shinyjs::useShinyjs()

# In the server, for a mounted cell:
shinyjs::disable("cars_car1_Price")
shinyjs::enable("cars_car1_Price")

The application must install/load shinyjs; it is not a required package dependency. Changes to the disabled attribute are detected and retained per cell. For a module, use local IDs with Shiny/shinyjs namespace mechanisms.

Disabling an interface is not authorization. Always check permissions on the server.

9. Indicators, errors, and localization 

colDef(editable = TRUE, editStatus = "icon", editStatusDuration = 2000)
colDef(editable = TRUE, editStatus = "text", editStatusDuration = 5000)
colDef(editable = TRUE, editStatus = "none")

By default, a neutral indicator appears while pending, a small green checkmark appears in the top-right corner for two seconds after acceptance, and an error appears below the field after rejection. Previous success and error messages disappear as soon as a new edit begins. The success timer starts at acceptance, not when the cell is remounted. editStatus = "none" hides indicators, but not error messages or accessible announcements.

language <- reactableLang(
  editLabel = "Edit {name}, row {rowId}",
  editPending = "Checking...",
  editSaved = "Saved",
  editUnavailable = "Editing is only available in Shiny",
  editInvalidDate = "Enter a valid date",
  rowAdd = "Add row",
  rowRemove = "-",
  rowRemoveLabel = "Remove row {rowId}",
  rowRemoveConfirm = "Remove row {rowId}?",
  rowAddPending = "Preparing row...",
  rowAdded = "Row added",
  rowRemoved = "Row removed",
  rowAddedLabel = "Added rows"
)
reactable(cars, rowId = "id", columns = columns, language = language)

Editor CSS variables: --rt-edit-success-color, --rt-edit-error-color, --rt-edit-pending-color, --rt-edit-indicator-top, --rt-edit-indicator-right. Indicator classes: .rt-cell-editor-indicator-saved, .rt-cell-editor-indicator-pending, .rt-cell-editor-indicator-error.

.rt-cell-editor {
  --rt-edit-success-color: #16733c;
  --rt-edit-indicator-top: 3px;
  --rt-edit-indicator-right: 4px;
}

Preserve accessible labels, contrast, and messages: color alone is not enough.

10. Tooltips: cells, inputs, and headers

reactableTooltip() 

reactableTooltip(content, placement = "top", maxWidth = 320, class = NULL)
  • content: text escaped automatically, htmltools tags, or trusted non-interactive HTML.
  • placement: preferred position: "top", "bottom", "left", or "right".
  • maxWidth: positive maximum width in CSS pixels.
  • class: additional CSS class on the popup.

The popup changes sides when needed and stays within the viewport. Plain text can be used directly in a rule without calling the constructor.

priceTooltip <- reactableTooltip(
  tagList(tags$b("Price"), tags$br(), "Positive amount, in thousands."),
  placement = "right",
  maxWidth = 280,
  class = "price-tooltip"
)

colDef(editable = TRUE, editor = "number", tooltip = priceTooltip, headerTooltip = "Vehicle price")
colDef(tooltip = function(value, index, name) paste(name, ": initial value", value))

tooltip also works on an ordinary cell. The R callback receives the value, R row index, and column name. It is evaluated at construction; its results follow stable keys when rowId is supplied. It is not recalculated after an edit or addition. Use a rule update for a dynamic tooltip. For new keys, a precalculated result from an existing row is not reused.

Table rules and precedence 

tooltips <- list(
  columns = list(Price = "Column help"),
  rows = list(car2 = "Shared tooltip for row car2"),
  cells = list(car1 = list(Price = priceTooltip), car3 = list(Notes = FALSE)),
  headers = list(Price = "Price in thousands")
)
reactable(cars, rowId = "id", columns = columns, tooltips = tooltips)
updateReactable("cars", tooltips = tooltips)

Cell precedence: input by ID > cell > row > table column > colDef default. headers does not follow row/cell rules; a header rule replaces its headerTooltip. rows and cells require rowId. Rules follow keys, including off-page keys or keys after data replacement. Aggregated group cells do not inherit rules from leaf cells.

updateReactableTooltip() 

updateReactableTooltip(session, inputId, tooltip)
updateReactableTooltip(session, "cars_car1_Price", "Higher-priority tooltip")
updateReactableTooltip(session, "cars_car1_Price", priceTooltip)
updateReactableTooltip(session, "cars_car1_Price", FALSE)

Targets a mounted native editor. It does not target an ordinary cell or an off-page cell; for those cases, use updateReactable(tooltips = ...). The ID override follows the cell through pagination, virtualization, and data replacement. Removing the row clears its individual override.

Hide, replace, or reset 

updateReactable("cars", tooltips = NULL)   # Leave unchanged
updateReactable("cars", tooltips = list()) # Clear rules and overrides, keep colDef defaults
updateReactable("cars", tooltips = list(cells = list(car1 = list(Price = FALSE))))

Any non-NULL list replaces all rules and clears ID overrides. A FALSE rule explicitly hides the tooltip, even if a lower-precedence level provides one. NULL cannot hide a rule and is not accepted by updateReactableTooltip(); use FALSE. There is no public helper to remove only one ID override and restore inheritance; sending the table rules again clears all such overrides.

Accessibility and CSS

Hover or keyboard focus displays the tooltip; Escape closes it. The pointer can move over the popup without closing it immediately. A disabled input gets a focusable container so its tooltip remains accessible. The tooltip and edit error coexist in aria-describedby. A tooltip does not replace the field’s accessible name or an essential instruction displayed on the page.

.price-tooltip {
  --rt-tooltip-background: #16324f;
  --rt-tooltip-color: #ffffff;
  border-radius: 6px;
}

The popup is placed under document.body, outside the table’s scrollable areas. Define its variables on :root, .rt-tooltip, or its own class, not only on a table ancestor. This prevents clipping, but affects descendant CSS selectors.

Do not put links, buttons, inputs, scripts, or htmlwidgets in a tooltip. The API accepts only trusted, non-interactive content; its controls are not an HTML sanitizer. Never pass user-provided HTML. For interactive content, use details or a popover.

11. Add and remove rows

rowActions 

reactable(
  cars, rowId = "id", columns = columns,
  rowActions = list(add = TRUE, remove = TRUE, removeDisabled = "car1")
)
updateReactable("cars", rowActions = list(add = FALSE, remove = TRUE, removeDisabled = "car1"))
updateReactable("cars", rowActions = list()) # Hide the controls

Enable rowActions at construction to use this feature; the add and remove options are independent. Each update replaces the options: an omitted option is not retained. removeDisabled contains stable keys represented as strings. Hiding the controls does not remove added rows or cancel a request that is already pending.

getReactableRowAction() 

getReactableRowAction(outputId, session = NULL)

Reactively returns NULL, then the most recent action:

  • Add: action = "add" and requestId.
  • Remove: action = "remove", requestId, rowId, and data, the removed contents.

Add asks the server to create a complete row and its key. Remove asks for confirmation in the browser, removes the row immediately, then notifies the server. Removal does not wait for server acceptance.

The server must check permissions and save the deletion, or restore its authorized data with updateReactable(data = ...) if it is rejected. Do not use client-submitted contents as the source of truth for a deletion; look up the row on the server by its key.

addReactableRow() 

addReactableRow(
  outputId, data = NULL, inputIds = NULL, requestId = NULL, error = NULL, session = NULL
)
newRow <- cars[1, , drop = FALSE]
newRow$id <- "car7" # Example: use a genuinely new key
newRow$Price <- 0

addReactableRow("cars", newRow, requestId = action$requestId)
addReactableRow(
  "cars", newRow, requestId = action$requestId,
  inputIds = c(Price = "price_car7")
)
addReactableRow("cars", requestId = action$requestId, error = "Creation rejected")

The two insertion examples are alternatives, not two calls for the same key. data must be a one-row data frame or matrix with all table columns, compatible types, and a new unique key. Validate the values and save them on the server before insertion. inputIds is a named vector or list keyed by editable columns; other IDs remain automatic. ID collisions, duplicate keys, and select values outside the choices are rejected.

requestId correlates the response with the add-button click. Without requestId, the server can initiate an addition on its own. An error response requires a requestId and cannot include data or inputIds.

Why do new rows stay at the bottom?

Added rows are pinned in a separate section at the bottom of each page, outside sorting, search, filters, grouping, and pagination. They do not occupy slots on regular pages. In virtual mode, their section has its own scrolling area so it remains accessible. However, they are included in the exposed data and selection; they are not merely decorative.

updateReactable("cars", data = saved())

This replacement integrates additions into the regular table behavior. It also cancels drafts and pending requests. Late responses to invalidated add requests are ignored. The inputIds overrides for additions are cleared; the usual ID rules then apply.

R renderers and precalculated details for original rows remain associated with their data after deletion. New rows do not have precalculated R details; JavaScript renderers can handle their values. Styles include .rt-row-add, .rt-row-remove, and .rt-row-action-cell.

12. Shiny modules

Use ns() in the UI, but use local IDs with the module session on the server.

carsUI <- function(id) {
  ns <- NS(id)
  tagList(
    actionButton(ns("price25"), "Price = 25"),
    reactableOutput(ns("cars"))
  )
}

carsServer <- function(id, data, columns) {
  moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {
    output$cars <- renderReactable(reactable(data, rowId = "id", columns = columns))
    observeEvent(input$price25, {
      updateNumericInput(session, "cars_car1_Price", value = 25)
      updateReactableTooltip(session, "cars_car1_Price", "Module tooltip")
    })
    observeEvent(getReactableEdit("cars", session), {
      edit <- getReactableEdit("cars", session)
      # Validate and save as in the complete example.
      # Then: resolveReactableEdit("cars", edit, session = session)
    }, ignoreInit = TRUE)
  })
}

For the "demo" module, the automatic DOM ID becomes demo-cars_car1_Price. Within the module, read input$cars_car1_Price and pass "cars_car1_Price" to updaters. For a custom ID "main_price", the DOM uses demo-main_price, while the local server uses input$main_price. The same principle applies to a custom prefix and addReactableRow(inputIds = ...).

The module snippet illustrates namespacing; it is not a complete saving server. Do not use the already namespaced DOM ID with session$sendInputMessage() from that same session.

13. updateReactable() and persistence 

updateReactable(
  outputId, data = NULL, sortBy = NULL, page = NULL, expanded = NULL,
  selected = NULL, meta = NULL, session = NULL,
  disabledInputs = NULL, rowActions = NULL, tooltips = NULL
)
Operation Effect
Sorting, filtering, pagination, virtualization Keys preserve drafts, errors, and dedicated overrides
resolveReactableEdit() Resolves only the corresponding submission
Native updater on a mounted cell Native value/options; does not replace R definitions
disabledInputs = list Replaces these rules and clears disabled ID overrides
tooltips = list Replaces these rules and clears tooltip ID overrides
rowActions = list Replaces the control options
data = newData Replaces data and cancels edits, drafts, and add requests

Replacing only the data preserves disabling and tooltip rules and overrides. Column rules built in R are not recalculated by this message. Page, selection, and expansion reset by default when data is replaced; sorting, filters, and grouping persist. To explicitly preserve the page or selection, use the corresponding parameters and check that their indices remain valid in the new data.

getReactableState("cars", "selected") returns R indices, not rowId keys. These positions can change after a deletion. To save an edit or delete a record, use the event key, never a displayed position.

14. Complete application: saving, observers, and updates

Copy this block into an R session with shiny, MASS, and reactableEdit available. It covers the six inputs, IDs, business-rule validation, an individual observer, updaters, disabling, tooltips, and row actions. Saving uses a session-specific reactiveVal(); it does not persist to disk. Authorization rules here are limited to protecting "car1".

library(shiny)
library(reactableEdit)

makeEditingGuideApp <- function() {
  cars <- MASS::Cars93[1:6, c("Manufacturer", "Model", "Type", "Price")]
  cars$id <- paste0("car", seq_len(nrow(cars)))
  cars$Manufacturer <- as.character(cars$Manufacturer)
  cars$Model <- as.character(cars$Model)
  cars$Type <- as.character(cars$Type)
  cars$Available <- TRUE
  cars$CheckedOn <- as.Date("2026-01-01")
  cars$Notes <- ""
  choices <- unique(cars$Type)

  columns <- list(
    id = colDef(show = FALSE),
    Model = colDef(tooltip = function(value) paste("Model:", value)),
    Manufacturer = colDef(editable = TRUE),
    Price = colDef(
      editable = TRUE, editor = "number", editorOptions = list(step = "any"),
      tooltip = "The server requires a positive price.", headerTooltip = "Price in thousands"
    ),
    Type = colDef(editable = TRUE, editor = "select", editorOptions = list(choices = choices)),
    Available = colDef(editable = TRUE, editor = "checkbox"),
    CheckedOn = colDef(editable = TRUE, editor = "date"),
    Notes = colDef(editable = TRUE, editor = "textarea", editorOptions = list(rows = 2))
  )

  ui <- fluidPage(
    h2("reactableEdit: editing and the server"),
    actionButton("price25", "First price = 25"),
    actionButton("disable_price", "Disable the first price"),
    actionButton("enable_price", "Re-enable the first price"),
    actionButton("change_tooltip", "Change the first cell's tooltip"),
    actionButton("integrate_additions", "Integrate additions"),
    p("ID-based commands assume car1 is visible. car1 is protected from deletion."),
    reactableOutput("cars"),
    h3("Latest individual input"),
    verbatimTextOutput("individual"),
    h3("Latest submission"),
    verbatimTextOutput("edit"),
    h3("Confirmed server data"),
    tableOutput("saved")
  )

  server <- function(input, output, session) {
    saved <- reactiveVal(cars)
    lastEdit <- reactiveVal(NULL)
    nextKey <- nrow(cars)
    tbl <- reactable(
      cars, rowId = "id", columns = columns,
      rowActions = list(add = TRUE, remove = TRUE, removeDisabled = "car1"),
      defaultPageSize = 4, searchable = TRUE,
      language = reactableLang(
        editPending = "Checking...", editSaved = "Saved",
        rowAdd = "Add", rowRemoveConfirm = "Remove row {rowId}?"
      )
    )
    output$cars <- renderReactable(tbl)
    output$saved <- renderTable(saved())
    output$edit <- renderPrint(lastEdit())
    individual <- reactiveVal(NULL)
    output$individual <- renderPrint(individual())

    observeEvent(input$cars_car1_Price, {
      individual(input$cars_car1_Price)
    }, ignoreInit = TRUE)

    observeEvent(getReactableEdit("cars"), {
      edit <- getReactableEdit("cars")
      lastEdit(edit)
      current <- saved()
      index <- match(edit$rowId, current$id)
      allowed <- c("Manufacturer", "Price", "Type", "Available", "CheckedOn", "Notes")
      reject <- function(message) resolveReactableEdit("cars", edit, error = message)
      scalar <- function(x) length(x) == 1 && !anyNA(x)
      if (is.na(index) || !edit$columnId %in% allowed) {
        reject("Unauthorized row or column.")
        return()
      }
      value <- edit$value
      valid <- switch(edit$columnId,
        Manufacturer = is.character(value) && scalar(value) && nzchar(trimws(value)),
        Price = is.numeric(value) && scalar(value) && is.finite(value) && value >= 0,
        Type = is.character(value) && scalar(value) && value %in% choices,
        Available = is.logical(value) && scalar(value),
        CheckedOn = is.character(value) && scalar(value) &&
          grepl("^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$", value),
        Notes = is.character(value) && scalar(value),
        FALSE
      )
      if (!valid) {
        reject("Invalid value: check the type and business rules.")
        return()
      }
      if (edit$columnId == "Manufacturer") value <- trimws(value)
      if (edit$columnId == "Price") value <- round(value, 2)
      if (edit$columnId == "CheckedOn") {
        value <- tryCatch(as.Date(value), error = function(e) as.Date(NA))
        if (is.na(value) || as.character(value) != edit$value) {
          reject("Invalid date.")
          return()
        }
      }
      current[[edit$columnId]][index] <- value
      saved(current)
      resolveReactableEdit("cars", edit, value = value)
    }, ignoreInit = TRUE)

    observeEvent(input$price25, {
      current <- saved()
      current$Price[current$id == "car1"] <- 25
      saved(current)
      updateNumericInput(session, "cars_car1_Price", value = 25)
    })
    observeEvent(input$disable_price, {
      updateReactableInput(session, "cars_car1_Price", disabled = TRUE)
    })
    observeEvent(input$enable_price, {
      updateReactableInput(session, "cars_car1_Price", disabled = FALSE)
    })
    observeEvent(input$change_tooltip, {
      updateReactable("cars", tooltips = list(
        cells = list(car1 = list(Price = reactableTooltip(tags$b("Updated tooltip"))))
      ))
    })
    observeEvent(input$integrate_additions, {
      updateReactable("cars", data = saved())
    })

    observeEvent(getReactableRowAction("cars"), {
      action <- getReactableRowAction("cars")
      current <- saved()
      if (identical(action$action, "add")) {
        nextKey <<- nextKey + 1L
        row <- cars[1, , drop = FALSE]
        row$id <- paste0("car", nextKey)
        row$Manufacturer <- "New"
        row$Model <- "New model"
        row$Price <- 0
        row$Available <- FALSE
        row$Notes <- ""
        saved(rbind(current, row))
        addReactableRow("cars", row, requestId = action$requestId)
      } else if (identical(action$action, "remove")) {
        if (identical(action$rowId, "car1") || !action$rowId %in% current$id) {
          showNotification("Unauthorized deletion.", type = "error")
          updateReactable("cars", data = current)
          return()
        }
        saved(current[current$id != action$rowId, , drop = FALSE])
      } else {
        showNotification("Unknown row action.", type = "error")
      }
    }, ignoreInit = TRUE)
  }
  shinyApp(ui, server)
}

app <- makeEditingGuideApp()
if (interactive()) runApp(app)

Suggested tests:

  1. Enter a negative price: a server error appears, with no change to the confirmed data.
  2. Enter 25.678: the value is normalized to 25.68 and accepted, then the checkmark appears.
  3. Enter a manufacturer name surrounded by spaces: the trimmed text is saved.
  4. Click “First price = 25”: the native input updates without a new global submission.
  5. Disable and re-enable the visible price; check the tooltip using the keyboard.
  6. Add a row: it remains at the bottom, even while searching.
  7. Click “Integrate additions”: the row joins the regular sorting and pagination.
  8. Delete another row; check the saved data.

To also test namespacing and virtualization with the repository demo:

source("@travail/app.R")
runEditingDemo(virtual = TRUE, module = TRUE)

Render the guide and extract the application

From the repository root, use RStudio’s Knit button or run:

rmarkdown::render("vignettes/edition.Rmd", output_dir = "@travail")
knitr::purl("vignettes/edition.Rmd", output = "@travail/edition-app.R", quiet = TRUE)
source("@travail/edition-app.R")

The HTML is readable documentation, not a standalone Shiny application. purl() extraction retains only the complete application, not the separate illustrative snippets. Rendering HTML requires rmarkdown and Pandoc; RStudio generally provides the latter.

15. Limitations and troubleshooting

  • Native editing and row actions require Shiny, use client-side processing, and do not support server = TRUE or .subRows.
  • Row actions do not support Crosstalk data. Ordinary tooltips can also be used in an HTML document without a server, but server callbacks and updates are unavailable there.
  • Native commands, ID-based disabling, and ID-based tooltips work only for mounted inputs.
  • Built-in saving, authentication, and multi-user conflict management are not provided.
  • There is no public API for partially updating off-page cell values; replace the data if needed.
  • Your application is not automatically guaranteed to meet WCAG requirements: check focus, contrast, zoom, screen readers, and touch interactions with your customizations.
Symptom Check
The cell remains pending Every validated edit waits for resolveReactableEdit()
The updater has no effect Check the ID, namespace, updater type, and whether the cell is mounted
Drafts disappear Look for a reactive rebuild or updateReactable(data = ...)
Multiple inputs have the same ID Check keys, prefixes, and constant callbacks
An old tooltip does not change after editing R tooltip callbacks are precalculated; send rules instead
A tooltip remains hidden Check for an ID override or a higher-priority FALSE rule
An input remains disabled after list() Check the colDef(inputDisabled = TRUE) default
The tooltip color does not change The popup is under body, not inside the table ancestor
A date has an unexpected type Native input: Date; global event: ISO string
Added rows are not sorted Integrate them with updateReactable(data = ...)

In R, also see ?reactableEdit::colDef, ?reactableEdit::getReactableEdit, ?reactableEdit::updateReactableInput, ?reactableEdit::reactableTooltip, and ?reactableEdit::addReactableRow.
